headline: GOLD MINERS SURGE 8-10% — Democrats Sweep Both Chambers; Gold to $4,136 as Dollar Crumbles on Midterm Result
snippet: Spot gold rallied to $4,136.60/oz on November 6 — its highest since October 22 — as the U.S. dollar tumbled to a one-month low after Democrats retained control of both Senate and House in Tuesday's midterm elections. Gold miners ETF surged more than 8% in a single session, with Newmont up 9.9%, Agnico Eagle up 9.67%, and Barrick adding 8.31%.

headline: CHINA REE TRUCE EXPIRES NOVEMBER 10 — No Renewal In Sight; USAR, MP Materials Surge on Supply Cliff
snippet: China's expanded rare earth export controls — temporarily suspended under a November 2025 truce — are set to expire without renewal on November 10, forcing Western automakers, defense contractors, and magnet producers to either hold sufficient inventory or face sharp price increases for dysprosium, terbium, and NdPr oxide. USA Rare Earth and MP Materials shares moved sharply higher as supply-cliff risk crystallized with just four days remaining.

headline: COEUR MINING Q3: REVENUE UP 77% TO $1 BILLION — 161K oz Gold, Copper Hits $6.65/lb; Costs Fall to $2,054/oz
snippet: Coeur Mining (NYSE: CDE) reported Q3 2026 revenue of approximately $1 billion — up 77% from $555 million in Q3 2025 — producing 161,400 ounces of gold at a realized price of $3,979/oz and 10.0 million pounds of copper at $6.65/lb, with all-in sustaining costs per gold ounce falling to $2,054 from $2,442 in the prior quarter.

headline: CHINA'S GLOBAL MINE GRAB ACCELERATES — Overseas Critical Mineral Stakes Tighten as REE Controls Near Nov. 10 End
snippet: Chinese state-owned and state-linked companies have accelerated overseas acquisitions of lithium, cobalt, and rare earth assets throughout 2026, raising Western governments' concern that Beijing is tightening its near-monopoly in both mine production and downstream processing even as its domestic export controls wind down — a strategy that leaves trade-deal concessions as the only near-term lever for Western buyers.

headline: CITI SLASHES LITHIUM FORECAST 40% — Surplus Through 2028 as EV Demand Growth Disappoints
snippet: Citigroup cut its two-year lithium price forecasts by as much as 40%, citing an emerging surplus expected to persist through 2028 as EV demand growth falls short of earlier projections and new supply from Australia, Latin America, and Africa continues to ramp — a bearish outlook that follows similar downgrades from Goldman Sachs and UBS earlier this year.

headline: GENESIS-VAULT A$12.6B MERGER ENTERS FINAL MONTH — Would Create ASX's Third-Largest Gold Producer
snippet: Genesis Minerals (ASX: GMD) and Vault Minerals (ASX: VAU) are on track to implement their A$12.6 billion scheme of arrangement in November 2026, following ACCC clearance in August; Vault shareholders receive 0.7629 Genesis shares plus A$0.475 cash per share, and the combined entity would become Australia's third-largest ASX-listed gold producer behind Newmont and Northern Star.

headline: CHINESE FIRM GRABS TIBET COPPER-LITHIUM RIGHTS — Xizang Gaozheng Secures Strategic Deposit; Shares Surge
snippet: Xizang Gaozheng Civil Explosives — a Chinese state-linked industrial firm — secured mining rights over the Mamupu copper-lithium deposit in Tibet, with its shares surging sharply on the announcement as markets interpreted the deal as confirmation of Beijing's accelerating grip on strategic battery-metal deposits at a time when Western buyers are scrambling for supply security.

headline: $144 MILLION DEPLOYED AT RESOLUTION COPPER — Rio-BHP Arizona Project Contracts Awarded; 50 New Jobs
snippet: Resolution Copper — the BHP and Rio Tinto joint venture targeting one of North America's largest undeveloped porphyry copper deposits in Arizona — awarded approximately $144 million in underground exploration and development contracts to two U.S. companies, with the work expected to create 50 new direct jobs as the project advances deeper development phases.

headline: VICTORY BATTERY METALS PIVOTS TO URANIUM — Acquires Historic Kachiwiss Deposit in Quebec, Keeps Battery Portfolio
snippet: Victory Battery Metals (CSE: VR3) signed an agreement to acquire uranium claims in Quebec including the historical Kachiwiss deposit, marking its entry into uranium exploration while maintaining its lithium and vanadium battery metals portfolio — the move aligns with a trend of junior miners adding uranium exposure as long-term uranium prices approach US$96/lb on structural supply deficits.

headline: FORTUNA DRILLS 1.9 g/t Au OVER 64m IN SENEGAL — Kabewest Initial Program Complete; 6 Rigs Pivot to New Targets
snippet: Fortuna Mining (TSX: FVI) completed a 45-hole, 10,524-metre initial drill program at the Kabewest prospect in its Bambadji project in Senegal, confirming geological continuity with the nearby Diamba Sud deposits at a headline intercept of 1.9 g/t gold over 64 metres plus 24.2 metres at 3.1 g/t; six drill rigs have now been redirected to the Wari and Latifa prospects for the next phase.

headline: Q2 METALS WINS QMEA DISCOVERY OF THE YEAR — Quebec Exploration Body Honours Chubb Gold Find; TSXV: QTWO
snippet: Q2 Metals (TSXV: QTWO) received the Quebec Mineral Exploration Association's Discovery of the Year Award for its Chubb gold discovery in the Chibougamau region — industry recognition from one of Canada's most credible provincial exploration bodies that validates the company's exploration success and signals institutional-quality geology for a junior that has drawn significant investor attention in 2025-2026.
